title: Strongly transcendental element over a reduced subring kills quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $R\subseteq S$ be a subring of a commutative ring, with $R$ and $S$ reduced (no nonzero nilpotent elements). Let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strongly-transcendental] (for the inclusion $R\to S$), and assume that $S$ is a finitely generated module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] over the subring $R[x]\subseteq S$ generated by $R$ and $x$ (so $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]). Then $R\to S$ is not quasi-finite at any prime ideal of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00Q2 (lemma-reduced-strongly-transcendental-not-quasi-finite, line 30714; its proof uses Lemmas 00Q0, 00Q1, 00PN)
